scope: PreBase Phase 3.18 Checkpoints B/C Tauri test review
behaviorsEnumerated: Plain Tauri exposes renderer automation and console capture while full-app test automation remains setupRequired.
Embedded WebDriver exposes full-native webview UI automation, not Tauri backend API access, and retains renderer console capture.
The rich tauri-plugin-wdio crate alone does not satisfy embedded WebDriver setup.
Setup adds only tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver, its prebase-testing feature, guarded Rust registration, and wdio-webdriver:default ACL.
Setup preserves an existing capability and creates a minimal capability when none exists.
Transaction failures on the first, second, and third writes restore completed work in reverse order.
Rollback deletes a newly created capability file.
Fixture frontendDist resolves to the dedicated web directory, never the fixture root or src-tauri/target.
The enabled fixture manifest, feature, and ACL contain only the embedded WebDriver plugin.
Live acceptance proves the Rust backend marker through backendInvoke=true and Hello, Ada.
weakOrMisleadingTestsFound: The already-enabled setup test accepted the removed tauri-plugin-wdio dependency and wdio:default ACL while still reporting a no-op.
The enabled detector test omitted supportsBackendApiAccess=false and supportsConsoleCapture=true.
Setup tests used substring/length assertions that could pass while obsolete plugin, feature, or ACL entries remained.
No transaction failure or rollback deletion behavior was covered.
Committed fixture tests did not constrain frontendDist or enumerate enabled WebDriver dependencies and ACLs.

newOrStrengthenedBehaviors: Enabled and setupRequired detector capability matrices.
Exact thin WebDriver Cargo dependency and feature membership.
Exact existing-capability preservation and minimal capability creation.
Thin-plugin idempotence without obsolete rich plugin or ACL.
First, second, and third transaction-write failures plus created-file deletion.
Both fixture frontendDist paths and enabled fixture plugin/feature/ACL truth.

intentionallyOmitted.reason: The live Tauri acceptance already executes the Rust command and records backendInvoke=true; a source-text assertion would not prove backend execution.
Existing DesktopWebDriverClient tests already cover loopback enforcement, session creation, execute errors, screenshot validation, and cancellation.

productionIssues: The current setup command does not type-check because its write callback does not normalize the file-service result to Promise<void>.
applyTauriTestingTransaction only records a write after it resolves; if a failed write partially mutates or creates its own resource before rejecting, that failed resource is not rolled back.
